scenes.heading: Pricing local service work: flat rate, hourly, or by job size

sents.d: Pricing local service work: flat rate, hourly, or by job size
Each pricing model fits different types of service work.
Hourly pricing is simple but can create tension if a job takes longer than expected, and doesn't reward efficiency — a faster provider earns less for the same completed work.

Flat-rate pricing based on job size or scope (per square foot, per room, per typical job type) gives customers upfront cost certainty and rewards efficient work, though it requires accurately estimating typical job time in advance.
Whichever model you use, building in a buffer for unexpected complications (and stating clearly what would trigger an additional charge) protects your margin without needing to renegotiate mid-job.

take: Use flat rates by job size, with a buffer for surprises.
